reason: Both plans satisfy all hard requirements (phases with percentages/entry criteria, correctly formatted RISK lines, no decommissioning bundled with the final migration batch, numeric halt thresholds, and the PHASES line), but Response B is slightly more operationally useful: it breaks phases into concrete sub-waves with percentages and timing, ties entry criteria to billing-cycle observation windows, and includes one additional distinct risk (silent data drift) alongside a more concrete Sev-1 definition in its halt criteria.
